baseline:
B
A vector is most intuitively understood as a geometric object possessing both a magnitude (length) and a direction. It exists within a vector space, where it can be combined with other vectors through addition and scalar multiplication.

C
A linear combination is the result of scaling two or more vectors by constant scalars and then adding them together. The expression `av + bw` is the general form for this operation on vectors v and w.

C
The 'span' of a set of vectors is defined as all possible vectors that can be formed by their linear combinations. For two non-parallel vectors in the 2D plane, their linear combinations can represent any vector in that entire plane.

B
This is the definition of linear dependence. It means one vector lies in the plane (or line) spanned by the other two, so the set of three vectors is redundant and does not span three-dimensional space.

C
A basis for a vector space is a set of vectors that are linearly independent and span the entire space. This means there is no redundancy in the set, and any vector in the space can be created by a unique linear combination of these basis vectors.
